message.content:
**A‑blues scale**

| Note | Interval from previous note | Semitone count |
|------|-----------------------------|----------------|
| A    | —                           | —              |
| C    | minor 3rd (3 semitones)     | 3              |
| D    | major 2nd (2 semitones)     | 2              |
| D♯   | diminished 5th (1 semitone) | 1              |
| E    | major 2nd (2 semitones)     | 2              |
| G    | minor 7th (3 semitones)     | 3              |
| A    | octave (8 semitones)        | 8              |

**Pattern of intervals (in semitones)**  
`3 – 2 – 1 – 3 – 2` (then the octave)

So the A‑blues scale consists of the notes:

**A – C – D – D♯ – E – G – A**

The “blue” note is the flattened fifth (D♯). This six‑note pattern is the core of the blues sound in any key.
